identificationModule.briefTitle: Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Combined With Immunotherapy and Anti-angiogenesis in Treating Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: A National Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized Controlled Study of Serplulimab Injection Combined With Bevacizumab to Improve the Complete Response Rate of Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Stage Intermediate and Low Rectal Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a multicenter, prospective, randomized phase II trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy combined with the PD-1 monoclonal antibody serplulimab and the anti-angiogenic agent bevacizumab in patients with previously untreated pMMR/MSS middle and low locally advanced rectal cancer. The study plans to enroll a total of 200 participants (100 in the experimental arm and 100 in the control arm).

interventions.name: serplulimab、bevacizumab
interventions.description: short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions → 2-week break → 2 cycles of FOLFOX + serplulimab + bevacizumab → 2 cycles of FOLFOX + serplulimab.

interventions.name: neoadjuvant chemoradiation therapy
interventions.description: short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions → 2-week break → 4 cycles of FOLFOX alone.

primaryOutcomes.description: Rate of patients who achieve clinical complete response

secondaryOutcomes.description: Rate of major pathological response assessed by postoperative pathology
Objective response rate assessed by RECIST 1.1 criteria
DFS was defined as the duration from the date of randomization to the date of the first recurrence (local, distant, or mixed) or death.
Time from randomization to death due to any cause
Proportion of patients who achieve organ preservation by choosing a watch-and-wait strategy or local excision after attaining clinical or pathological complete response
Neoadjuvant rectal score assessed by postoperative pathology
Quality of life score during treatment and follow-up
Incidence of adverse events (AEs), incidence of abnormal laboratory values, and dose adjustments during treatment and follow-up
